questions.question: The removal procedure of a Supreme Court judge is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Impeachment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The removal of a **Supreme Court judge** is a rigorous process governed by **Article 124(4)** of the **Constitution of India** and the **Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968**, commonly known as **Impeachment**.
 
• A judge can be removed from office only on the grounds of **proved misbehaviour** or **incapacity**.
 
• The process begins with a removal motion signed by at least **100 members** in the **Lok Sabha** or **50 members** in the **Rajya Sabha**, which is then submitted to the Speaker or Chairman.
 
• If the motion is admitted, a **three-member committee** is constituted to investigate the charges. This committee includes a **Supreme Court judge**, a **Chief Justice of a High Court**, and a **distinguished jurist**.
 
• For the removal to be effective, the motion must be passed by each House of **Parliament** with a **special majority**: a majority of the **total membership** of the House and a majority of not less than **two-thirds** of the members present and voting.
 
• Following the passage of the motion in both Houses during the same session, an address is presented to the **President**, who then issues the formal order for removal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial Review**

 
 
• This is the power of the **Judiciary** to examine the validity of laws passed by the **Legislature** and actions taken by the **Executive**.
 
• It ensures that all state actions conform to the **Constitution**, as supported by **Articles 13, 32, 131-136, 143, 226, and 246**.
 
 
 
• **Recall**
 
 
• A mechanism of direct democracy where voters can remove an elected official before their term ends; this does not apply to the **Indian Judiciary**.
 
 
 
• **Dismissal by President**
 
 
• While the **President** signs the final order, they cannot dismiss a **Supreme Court judge** unilaterally or at their pleasure. The **Independence of the Judiciary** is protected by requiring the **Parliamentary** process first.

questions.question: Which Committee recommended Fundamental Duties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swaran Singh Committee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Swaran Singh Committee** was appointed by the **Indian National Congress** government in **1976** during the **National Emergency** (1975−1977).
 
• The primary objective of the committee was to make recommendations about **Fundamental Duties**, the necessity of which was felt to balance the **Fundamental Rights** of citizens with their obligations to the state.
 
• The committee suggested the inclusion of a separate chapter on **Fundamental Duties** in the Constitution, emphasizing that citizens should be aware that they have certain duties to perform while enjoying their rights.
 
• Accepting these recommendations, the Parliament enacted the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**, which added a new **Part IV-A** and **Article 51A** to the **Constitution of India**.
 
• Initially, the **Swaran Singh Committee** suggested **eight** duties, but the **42nd Amendment** actually included **ten**; later, the **11th Fundamental Duty** was added by the **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajamannar Committee**:

 
 
• Appointed by the **Tamil Nadu Government** in **1969** under the chairmanship of **Dr. P.V. Rajamannar**.
 
• It was tasked with examining the entire gamut of **Centre-State relations** and suggesting amendments to the Constitution to secure greater autonomy for the states.
 
 
 
• **Sarkaria Committee**:
 
 
• Set up in **1983** by the Central Government of India, headed by **Justice R.S. Sarkaria**.
 
• Its mandate was to examine the relationship and balance of power between **State and Central governments** and suggest changes within the framework of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Balwant Rai Mehta Committee**:
 
 
• Appointed in **January 1957** to examine the working of the **Community Development Programme** and the **National Extension Service**.
 
• It recommended the establishment of the scheme of **Democratic Decentralization**, which eventually became known as **Panchayati Raj**.

questions.question: Who is the author of the treatise Raga Tarangini?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pt. Lochan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pt. Lochan** is the esteemed author of the Sanskrit musical treatise titled **Raga Tarangini**, which is a pivotal work in the history of **Hindustani Classical Music**.
 
• Though there is historical debate regarding its exact timeline, the work is widely attributed to the **15th century** (around 1450-1500 AD) and reflects the musical landscape of the **Mithila** region.
 
• The primary significance of **Raga Tarangini** lies in its systematic **classification of Ragas**. Lochan was among the first to categorize Ragas under parental scales known as **Melas** or **Thaats**.
 
• He established a system consisting of **12 Melas** (parental scales), which provided a structural foundation for the organization of countless derivative Ragas (Janya Ragas).
 
• The **12 Thaats** identified by Lochan include **Bhairavi, Todi, Gauri, Karnat, Kedar, Yaman, Sarang, Megha, Dhanashri, Purvi, Mukhari, and Deepak**.
 
• The text also discusses the **Shuddha** and **Vikrit** notes of that period, describing a scale of **12 notes** comprising 7 natural and 5 modified notes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pt. Ahobal**:

 
 
• The author of **Sangeet Parijat**, written in the **17th century** (approximately 1665 AD).
 
• He is famous for being the first to describe the **exact locations of 12 notes** on the string of a **Veena** using mathematical proportions.
 
 
 
• **Pt. Sharngadeva**:
 
 
• The author of **Sangeet Ratnakara**, composed in the **13th century**.
 
• Often referred to as the **Saptadhyayi**, this work is considered the most comprehensive authority on Indian music, bridging **ancient (Marga)** and **medieval (Desi)** traditions.
 
 
 
• **Pt. Bhatkhande** (Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande):
 
 
• A **modern musicologist** who revolutionized Hindustani music by introducing the current **10 Thaat system**.
 
• His major works include **Hindustani Sangeet Paddhati** and the **Kramik Pustak Malika** series.

questions.question: What does the mass of an object measure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Its inertia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mass** is a fundamental property of matter that represents the amount of substance present in an object. It is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has magnitude but no direction.
 
• **Inertia** is the inherent tendency of any physical object to resist changes in its state of motion or rest. This concept is central to **Newton's First Law of Motion**, often referred to as the **Law of Inertia**.
 
• The mass of an object is the **quantitative measure** of its inertia. A body with a larger mass requires a greater **unbalanced force** to change its velocity (acceleration) compared to a body with a smaller mass.
 
• The **SI unit** of mass is the **kilogram (kg)**. Unlike weight, the mass of an object remains **constant** regardless of its location in the universe or the gravitational pull acting upon it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Weight**:

 
 
• It is the **gravitational force** exerted on an object by a celestial body like Earth.
 
• It is calculated as **Weight = Mass × acceleration due to gravity (g)**.
 
• The **SI unit** is the **Newton (N)**, and it changes depending on the strength of the local gravitational field.
 
 
 
• **Volume**:
 
 
• This identifies the amount of **three-dimensional space** that a substance or object occupies.
 
• For solids, it is typically measured in **cubic meters (m³)**, while for liquids, it is measured in **liters (L)**.
 
 
 
• **Density**:
 
 
• It is defined as the **mass per unit volume** of a material.
 
• The formula is **Density = Mass / Volume**, and its SI unit is **kg/m³**. It indicates how tightly matter is packed within an object.

questions.question: When is the longest day in the Northern Hemisphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Summer Solstice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Summer Solstice** marks the point in the **Earth's orbit** where the **Northern Hemisphere** is tilted at its maximum angle of **23.5 degrees** toward the **Sun**.
 
• This astronomical event occurs annually on **June 20, 21, or 22**, with **June 21** being the most frequent date.
 
• During the solstice, the **Sun** reaches its highest position in the sky at solar noon for observers located at the **Tropic of Cancer** (23.5° N latitude).
 
• The Northern Hemisphere experiences the **longest duration of daylight** and the **shortest night** of the year because a larger portion of the hemisphere is exposed to sunlight due to the **axial tilt**.
 
• Geographically, areas within the **Arctic Circle** experience the **Midnight Sun**, where the Sun does not set for a full 24-hour period.
 
• In contrast, the **Southern Hemisphere** simultaneously experiences its **Winter Solstice**, resulting in its shortest day and longest night of the year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Winter Solstice**:

 
 
• Typically occurs on **December 21 or 22** in the Northern Hemisphere.
 
• The **North Pole** is tilted farthest from the **Sun**, which is directly over the **Tropic of Capricorn** (23.5° S).
 
• It identifies the **shortest day** and the official start of astronomical winter.
 
 
 
• **Equinoxes**:
 
 
• **Vernal Equinox**: Occurs around **March 20-21**, marking the start of spring when the **Sun** crosses the **Equator** moving north.
 
• **Autumnal Equinox**: Happens around **September 22-23**, signaling the beginning of autumn as the Sun moves south across the Equator.
 
• During an **Equinox**, day and night are approximately **12 hours** each across the entire planet.

questions.question: Which nation landed the first rover on the far side of the Moon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**China**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **China** made history by becoming the first nation to successfully achieve a soft landing on the **far side of the Moon** through its **Chang'e 4** mission.
 
• The spacecraft landed on **January 3, 2019**, within the **Von Kármán crater**, which is situated in the **South Pole-Aitken (SPA) Basin**, the largest and oldest impact crater on the Moon.
 
• The mission successfully deployed the **Yutu-2** (Jade Rabbit-2) rover, which became the first robotic vehicle to traverse the rugged and geologically distinct terrain of the lunar hemisphere that faces away from Earth.
 
• Since the Moon's bulk blocks direct radio communication with Earth, **China** launched the **Queqiao** relay satellite to the **Earth-Moon L2 Lagrange point** to facilitate data transmission between the rover and ground control.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Technological and Scientific Objectives**:

 
 
• The **Yutu-2** rover is equipped with **Lunar Penetrating Radar (LPR)** to investigate the sub-surface structure and **Visible and Near-Infrared Imaging Spectrometers (VNIS)** to identify mineral compositions.
 
• The mission conducts **low-frequency radio astronomical observations**, taking advantage of the far side's unique radio-quiet environment, shielded from Earth's electromagnetic interference.
 
 
 
• **Other Lunar Missions**:
 
 
• **USA**: NASA's **Apollo** missions (1969−1972) achieved the first human landings, but all were located on the **lunar near side**.
 
• **India**: The **Chandrayaan-3** mission landed the **Pragyan** rover near the **Lunar South Pole** in August 2023, making India the first to reach that specific region, though not the far side.
 
• **Russia**: The **Soviet Union** obtained the first-ever images of the far side in 1959 with **Luna 3**, but did not deploy a rover there.

questions.question: Who is the first individual Olympic gold medallist for India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abhinav Bindra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Abhinav Bindra** scripted history by becoming the first Indian athlete to win an **individual gold medal** at the Olympic Games.
 
• He achieved this milestone in the **Men's 10m Air Rifle** shooting event at the **2008 Beijing Olympics**.
 
• In the high-pressure final, Bindra shot a total score of **700.5**, which included a remarkable **10.8** on his final shot to overtake his competitors.
 
• Before this achievement, India had only won gold medals in **Field Hockey**, which is a team sport, making Bindra the pioneer of individual success at the highest level.
 
• His victory ended a **28-year** gold medal drought for India at the Olympics, the previous gold having been won by the hockey team in **1980**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Milkha Singh**:

 
 
• Commonly known as the **Flying Sikh**, he was a legendary sprinter who represented India in multiple Olympics.
 
• He famously missed out on a medal by **0.1 seconds**, finishing fourth in the **400m** race at the **1960 Rome Olympics**.
 
 
 
• **Leander Paes**:
 
 
• He is a world-renowned tennis player who won the **bronze medal** in the **Men's Singles** event at the **1996 Atlanta Olympics**.
 
• This was the first individual Olympic medal for India in **44 years**, following K.D. Jadhav's bronze in **1952**.
 
 
 
• **Sushil Kumar**:
 
 
• A highly successful **freestyle wrestler** who won two consecutive individual Olympic medals.
 
• He secured a **bronze medal** at the **2008 Beijing Olympics** and a **silver medal** at the **2012 London Olympics**.

questions.question: In T20 cricket, how many fielders are allowed outside the 30-yard circle after the powerplay?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Twenty20 (T20)** cricket, fielding restrictions are implemented to encourage aggressive batting and balance the game. The innings is divided into a **Powerplay** phase and a non-Powerplay phase.
 
• The **Powerplay** consists of the first **6 overs** of a standard 20-over innings. During this period, a maximum of **2 fielders** are allowed to be stationed outside the **30-yard (27.43 meters) circle**.
 
• Following the completion of the **Powerplay** (from the start of the **7th over** until the final delivery of the **20th over**), the restrictions are relaxed. A maximum of **5 fielders** are permitted to be placed outside the **30-yard circle**.
 
• These regulations are strictly enforced by the **International Cricket Council (ICC)** for international matches and are widely adopted by various domestic leagues like the **IPL** and **Big Bash**.
 
• Failure to maintain the required number of fielders inside the circle at the moment of delivery results in the **Umpire** calling a **No Ball**, which grants the batting team a **Free Hit**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **On-Side Restrictions**:

 
 
• Irrespective of the phase of the innings, no more than **5 fielders** are allowed on the **leg side** (on-side) of the batsman at any given time.
 
• Furthermore, no more than **2 fielders** are allowed behind the popping crease on the **leg side**.
 
 
 
• **Slow Over Rate Penalty**:
 
 
• According to updated **ICC Playing Conditions**, if a fielding team fails to start their final over by the scheduled cut-off time, they must bring an additional fielder inside the circle.
 
• In such cases, only **4 fielders** are allowed outside the **30-yard circle** for the remaining duration of the innings.
 
 
 
• **Rain-Curtailed Matches**:
 
 
• If a match is shortened due to rain, the duration of the **Powerplay** is adjusted proportionally to the total number of overs assigned to the innings.

questions.question: In which year was the Deccan Airways was nationalised?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1953**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The civil aviation sector in India underwent a massive structural change with the enactment of the **Air Corporations Act, 1953**, which aimed to consolidate the fragmented airline industry.
 
• **Deccan Airways**, one of the premier private airlines of that era, was officially nationalized on **August 1, 1953**, under the provisions of this legislation.
 
• Following the nationalization process, **Deccan Airways** was merged along with seven other domestic airlines to form the state-owned **Indian Airlines Corporation** (IAC).
 
• The primary objective of this nationalization was to create a unified domestic carrier that could provide standard safety, better operational efficiency, and comprehensive connectivity across **Independent India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deccan Airways Limited**:

 
 
• It was established in **1945** as a joint venture between the **Nizam of Hyderabad** and **Tata Airlines**.
 
• The airline played a crucial role in the **Deccan** region, operating key routes connecting **Hyderabad** to **Madras**, **Bombay**, and **Delhi**.
 
 
 
• **The Eight Nationalized Entities**:
 
 
• The **1953** nationalization involved eight major airlines: **Air India**, **Air Services of India**, **Airways (India)**, **Bharat Airways**, **Deccan Airways**, **Himalayan Aviation**, **Indian National Airways**, and **Kalinga Airlines**.
 
 
 
• **Post-Nationalization Landscape**:
 
 
• The industry was bifurcated into two specialized corporations: **Indian Airlines** for all domestic and regional flights and **Air India International** for long-distance overseas operations.
 
• **J.R.D. Tata** was appointed as the chairman of the international wing, ensuring that the expertise of private pioneers was retained within the government framework.

questions.question: Kartarpur is situated near which river?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ravi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kartarpur** is located in the **Shakargarh Tehsil** of the **Narowal District** in the **Punjab province** of **Pakistan**.
 
• The town is situated on the **right bank** of the **Ravi River**, one of the primary transboundary rivers of the **Indus River System**.
 
• It holds immense religious significance as it was founded by **Guru Nanak Dev Ji**, the first Guru of Sikhism, in **1522**.
 
• **Guru Nanak** spent the final 18 years of his life in Kartarpur, where he established a **communal kitchen (Langar)** and practiced **farming** on the fertile plains of the **Ravi**.
 
• The **Gurdwara Darbar Sahib Kartarpur** is built at the site where Guru Nanak is believed to have breathed his last.
 
• The **Kartarpur Corridor**, inaugurated in **November 2019**, connects this shrine to the **Dera Baba Nanak** shrine in **Gurdaspur**, India, crossing the **Ravi River** to facilitate visa-free travel for pilgrims.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ravi River**:

 
 
• Known in ancient India as **Purushni** or **Irawati**.
 
• It originates in the **Bara Bhangal** area of **Kangra district** in **Himachal Pradesh** and flows through the **Chamba Valley**.
 
• It serves as a major source of irrigation for the **Bari Doab** region.
 
 
 
• **Sutlej River**:
 
 
• The longest of the five rivers of **Punjab**, originating from **Lake Rakshastal** in Tibet.
 
• It enters India through the **Shipki La** pass and is the site of the **Bhakra-Nangal Dam**.
 
 
 
• **Ganga and Yamuna**:
 
 
• The **Ganga** flows through the **Indo-Gangetic Plain** of North and East India, while the **Yamuna** is its largest tributary originating from the **Yamunotri Glacier**.
 
• Neither river flows through the **Punjab region** where Kartarpur is situated.

questions.question: Which app has been developed by the ICAR-Central Institute of Freshwater Aquaculture (CIFA) in December 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rangeen Machhli**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **ICAR-Central Institute of Freshwater Aquaculture (CIFA)**, located in **Bhubaneswar**, officially launched the **Rangeen Machhli** mobile application in **December 2024** to boost the **ornamental fisheries** sector in India.
 
• The app is designed as a one-stop digital solution for **hobbyists**, **entrepreneurs**, and **fish farmers**, providing essential information on the breeding, rearing, and management of various **ornamental fish species**.
 
• It features a comprehensive database covering over **80 species** of colorful fish, detailed modules on **water quality maintenance**, and scientific protocols for **feed management** to ensure high survival rates in captive environments.
 
• The application plays a pivotal role in the **Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)** by promoting **innovation** and **technology infusion** in the aquaculture domain.
 
• One of its core functions is the **Find a Shop** feature, which helps users locate nearby **aquarium stores** and suppliers, thereby strengthening the **supply chain** and market connectivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ICAR-CIFA**:

 
 
• Established in **1987**, it is a premier research institute under the **Indian Council of Agricultural Research** focusing on **freshwater aquaculture** research and development.
 
• The institute has been instrumental in developing high-yielding varieties like the **Jayanti Rohu** and various **breeding technologies** for carps and catfishes.
 
 
 
• **Ornamental Fisheries Sector**:
 
 
• Often described as **'Living Jewels'**, this sector is a significant foreign exchange earner and provides sustainable **livelihood opportunities** for rural women and urban youth.
 
• The **Rangeen Machhli** app supports the **Blue Economy** by reducing the knowledge gap and encouraging **indigenous production** of high-value species like **Goldfish**, **Gourami**, and **Angel Fish**.
 
• The app is available in multiple languages, including **Hindi** and **English**, to ensure wider accessibility across different geographical regions of India.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct as per the given information? "It is the rhythmic rise and fall of ocean water twice in a day. It is caused by the strong gravitational pull exerted by the sun and the moon on the earth's surface."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tides** are the periodic and **rhythmic rise and fall** of the sea level, occurring typically twice in a **lunar day** (approximately 24 hours and 50 minutes).
 
• This phenomenon is primarily driven by the **gravitational forces** exerted by the **Moon** and the **Sun** on the **Earth**, combined with the **centrifugal force** generated by the Earth's rotation.
 
• The **Moon** has a more significant influence on tides than the Sun because of its proximity to Earth; its pull creates a **tidal bulge** in the ocean water on the side facing the Moon and the side directly opposite.
 
• When the water reaches its highest point on the shore, it is termed **High Tide**, while the lowest point of recession is called **Low Tide**.
 
• During **Full Moon** and **New Moon** days, the Sun, Moon, and Earth align in a straight line, resulting in the highest tides known as **Spring Tides**. Conversely, when the Sun and Moon are at right angles, **Neap Tides** occur, which have a lower range.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tsunami**:

 
 
• A series of extremely long-wavelength ocean waves caused by massive **underwater disturbances** such as **earthquakes**, volcanic eruptions, or landslides.
 
• Unlike the predictable nature of tides, these are sudden and often **catastrophic events** not caused by gravitational pulls.
 
 
 
• **Cyclone**:
 
 
• A weather system characterized by **low atmospheric pressure** at the center and strong winds rotating inwards.
 
• In the **Northern Hemisphere**, the rotation is counter-clockwise, and it brings intense **rainfall** and storm surges.
 
 
 
• **Western Disturbance**:
 
 
• An **extratropical storm** originating in the **Mediterranean region** that travels eastward.
 
• It is responsible for sudden winter rain in the **northwestern parts** of the Indian subcontinent, which is vital for **Rabi crops**.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is correct regarding CENSUS? I. The first modern population census in India was conducted between 1865 and 1872. II. Next census in India will be conducted by 2028.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The history of the modern census in India began under the British administration. The first population census was conducted in a non-synchronous manner in different parts of the country between **1865** and **1872**. This effort culminated in **1872** under the viceroyalty of **Lord Mayo**, though it did not cover the entire territory of India simultaneously. Hence, statement I is correct.
 
• In India, the census is typically a **decennial** exercise, meaning it occurs every **ten years**. The last census was conducted in **2011**. While the **2021 Census** was delayed indefinitely due to the **COVID-19 pandemic**, there is no official government notification or statutory mandate stating that the next census will specifically be conducted by **2028**. Projections and administrative discussions vary, but it does not represent a fixed official schedule. Hence, statement II is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Historical Evolution**:

 
 
• The first **synchronous census** (conducted all at once across the country) took place in **1881** under the guidance of **W.C. Plowden**, the **Census Commissioner**, during the tenure of **Lord Ripon**.
 
• Since **1881**, the census has been conducted uninterruptedly every ten years until the **2021** cycle was disrupted.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Framework**:
 
 
• The responsibility of conducting the census rests with the **Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner**, which operates under the **Ministry of Home Affairs**, Government of India.
 
• The exercise is legally backed by the **Census Act, 1948**, which provides the framework for data collection and ensures the **confidentiality** of information provided by citizens.
 
• The **2011 Census** was the **15th** census of India and the **7th** since independence.

questions.question: 'Bayalata' is a folk dance of which of the following Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Bayalata** is a traditional **folk theater** and dance performance native to the state of **Karnataka**, specifically popular in its rural and coastal regions.
 
• The term is derived from the **Kannada** language, where **Bayalu** means an open field and **Ata** means a play or performance, indicating its traditional staging in open-air venues like harvest fields or temple grounds.
 
• The performance marks the end of the **harvest season** and serves as a medium for both religious devotion and community entertainment.</li&g

questions.question: Which of the following is the most popular traditional dance of the tribes of Kalahandi district in Odisha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghumura**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ghumura** is a traditional folk dance originating from the **Kalahandi district** of **Odisha**, characterized by its vibrant music and rhythmic complexity.
 
• The dance is named after the **Ghumura**, a unique **pitcher-shaped drum** made of **clay** with a mouth covered by the skin of a **Godhi** (monitor lizard).
 
• Historically categorized as a **war dance**, it was used to motivate soldiers in ancient **Kalinga**; archaeological evidence of this dance form is found in the carvings of the **Konark Sun Temple**.
 
• Literary references to the Ghumura instrument appear in ancient texts such as the **Mahabharata** and the **Chandi Purana**, where it is described as being used by deities.
 
• It is traditionally performed during major festivals like **Nuakhai** and **Dasahara**, where dancers move in circular formations wearing **colorful turbans** and traditional **Odishi** attire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kikli**:

 
 
• This is a lively folk dance of **Punjab**, primarily performed by young girls.
 
• It involves two performers crossing their arms and holding hands while whirling rapidly in a circle.
 
 
 
• **Luddi**:
 
 
• A celebratory folk dance from the **Punjab region** (Sutlej and Chenab river areas), often performed by men.
 
• It is performed to celebrate **victory** or agricultural success, involving rhythmic clapping and finger snapping.
 
 
 
• **Singhi Chaam**:
 
 
• A significant **mask dance** from the state of **Sikkim**, also known as the **Snow Lion Dance**.
 
• Performers dress in white fur costumes to represent the mythical **Snow Lion**, which is a symbol of **purity** and a guardian of **Mount Khangchendzonga**.

questions.question: In which of the following year did Milkha Singh win a gold medal in Asian Games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1958**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Milkha Singh**, one of India’s greatest track and field athletes, achieved his first major international success at the **1958 Asian Games** held in **Tokyo, Japan**.
 
• During this edition of the games, he won **two gold medals** in the **200-meter** and **400-meter** sprint events, establishing his dominance in Asian athletics.
 
• In the **200m** final, he clocked a time of **21.6 seconds**, while in the **400m** event, he secured the top spot with a timing of **47.0 seconds**, defeating top competitors from across the continent.
 
• His performance at the **1958 Asian Games** served as a precursor to his success at the **Commonwealth Games** later that same year, where he became a household name.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Milkha Singh’s Sporting Career and Legacy**:

 
 
• **Commonwealth Games**: In **1958**, he won the gold medal in the **440-yard** race at the **Cardiff Commonwealth Games**, making him the first athlete from independent India to win an individual gold at the event.
 
• **1962 Asian Games**: Singh continued his winning streak at the **Jakarta Asian Games**, securing gold medals in both the **400-meter** race and the **4×400-meter relay**.
 
• **Rome Olympics 1960**: He is famously remembered for his **fourth-place finish** in the **400m final**, where he missed the bronze medal by **0.1 seconds** but set a national record of **45.73 seconds** that stood for decades.
 
• **The Flying Sikh**: This legendary nickname was bestowed upon him by **General Ayub Khan** of Pakistan in **1960** after he defeated **Abdul Khaliq** in a highly publicized race in Lahore.
 
• **Honors**: For his monumental contributions to Indian sports, he was awarded the **Padma Shri**, India’s fourth-highest civilian award, in **1959**.
 
• **Autobiography**: His life journey, including his struggle during the Partition, is detailed in his book titled **'The Race of My Life'**.
